newsitem.title: EGYPT: Amoco may export Egyptian gas to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Amoco may export Egyptian gas to Turkey.

text.p: The U.S. oil company Amoco may take part in a project to export Egyptian natural gas to Turkey, Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said in an interview published on Sunday.
Banbi told the government newspaper al-Ahram that gas export negotiations with Turkey were more advanced than those with Israel but gave no details to support this.

"There is a dialogue with several countries but the country with which we have reached the most advanced stage in negotiations is Turkey, not Israel, although Israel is closer geographically," he said.
"We have negotiated and have almost reached an understood framework with Turkey," he added.
Banbi told Reuters last month that differences between Egypt and Israel over the Middle East peace process would not derail long-term plans to supply Israel with natural gas.
He said a draft agreement was being prepared in Egypt, while Israel has an international company to study gas pipeline routes and establish a master plan for gas utilisation in Israel.
In contrast talks with Turkey appeared not to have reached the technical stage.
Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan will come to Egypt this week for talks on Turkey's possible purchase of natural gas.
Kutan will discuss buying gas from Egypt through either a pipeline under the Mediterranean or through tankers in liquefied natural gas (LNG) form, Turkish officials said.
Banbi said Egyptian gas exports would come up at this week's Middle East and North Africa economic conference, which opens in Cairo on Tuesday.
"(The head of Amoco) will speak about his participation with Egypt in exporting the gas to Turkey," Banbi added.

Amoco officials in Cairo were not available to comment on Sunday but one Amoco executive told Reuters in August: "Given the potential (for gas exports) we are also looking at liquefaction for export by tanker to Europe."

Banbi also said an announcement would be made at the conference on a decision by the U.S. company Phillips to build a propylene plant in Egypt. Officials at Phillips Petroleum Egypt office said they did not know of the plan.
Egypt is in discussions with Dow Chemical, Banbi added, on a vast petroleum complex including a liquefaction plant for gas exports and a port.
